text:
sara: Noticed odd behavior after the rbac split deploy — some users with only Viewer see the Edit button on Project > Acme. Can anyone confirm?

mike: I can reproduce on staging. Steps:
1) login as viewer@acme
2) go to Projects -> Acme -> Settings
3) Edit button visible. Clicking sometimes 403s, sometimes opens modal.

anya: Screenshot or clip? :eyes:

mike: small clip uploaded: https://internal.captures/acme-edit-flaky.mp4

kyler: Dug into auth traces. There's a legacy fallback that appears to grant editor-like access when KMS key-owner metadata matches. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-19T20:59:41Z] auth.check user=viewer@acme action=project.update resource=proj:acme
[decision] allow=false via=role-matrix
[decision] legacy_override role_alias=editor_v1 reason=kms_key_owner match
[final] allow=true audit_id=auth-9a1c
```

sara: That override shouldn't convert a Viewer to Editor for console actions. The split migration intended strict deny unless explicit grant.

mike: Looks like aggregator ORs legacyFallback with new checks. So legacy_binding=true || roleMatrix=true -> allows. Should be precedence: explicit deny should win and legacy fallback only consulted when nothing explicit.

anya: UX fallout: buttons visible create false affordances. Users click, get 403 — bad experience and security noise. We should hide Update/Edit until server permission probe returns.

kyler: Agree. I'll prepare a small auth-lib fix: change aggregator to respect explicit-deny precedence and ensure legacyFallback only evaluated if no decisive result. Also remove kms_key_owner -> editor grant mapping for console-level actions.

mike: Immediate mitigation: can roll the rbac-split flag back. Ops approval? I can queue via rolloutbot.

rolloutbot: rolloutbot: rbac-split flag: disable request queued by mike. ETA ~45s.

sara: Good. Also need tests: unit for role invariants (viewer must not get edit affordance) and an e2e that verifies UI hide/show logic.

kyler: I'll add audit logging on any legacy_override occurrences and run a query across auth_traces for the past 30 days: 
```
SELECT * FROM auth_traces WHERE legacy_override IS NOT NULL AND action ILIKE '%update%';
```
Schedule job to run and dump results to the SEC ticket.

mike: Rolling flag now. rolloutbot: rbac-split disabled at 2026-03-19T21:02:12Z :white_check_mark:

anya: I'll add a client-side guard: hide edit button until permission probe resolves. Push canary to staging in 20m. That reduces clicks while server fix lands.

sara: Owners:
- flag rollback: mike (done)
- auth aggregator fix + tests: kyler
- UI guard + e2e: anya
- postmortem + legacy-alias audit: sara

mike: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/auth/pull/582 (explicit-deny precedence, test for viewer invariants).

kyler: Audit query job scheduled. If we find other resources where kms_owner grants elevated console perms we'll add them to the blocklist and notify infra owners.

sara: Filing SEC-4821 for tracking and customer comms. Notifying support to surface any reported flakiness.

mike: SEC-4821 updated with rollback + linked PRs + canary plan.

anya: Quick note: we should also review the migration script that generated legacy alias mappings. There might be other alias->grant assumptions baked in.

kyler: Agreed. I'll add a migration-audit checklist item: verify no key_owner mappings grant non-cryptographic console permissions.

sara: Thanks all. Once kyler's patch passes tests let's do a staged rollout: staging -> single region prod -> global. Keep the flag off until audited.

rolloutbot: ticket SEC-4821 updated by mike: "rbac-split disabled, auth-agg fix in PR, UI guard added; audit job scheduled"
